rationale: Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is essentially Sloan accruals bundled with standard earnings-quality/quality-minus-junk components, and the nested SUMRANK silently gives the accrual leg 50% weight versus 25% each to stability and trend, so any result will be hard to attribute to the claimed interaction.

The conditional logic is economically sensible, but multiplying by a 0/1 indicator collapses all trend-negative firms to exactly zero, placing them in the middle of the cross-section indistinguishably from firms with genuinely neutral accruals, which makes the sort non-monotonic and confounds "signal off" with "signal neutral."

The signal-to-noise framing is a defensible refinement of the accrual measure rather than a pure rediscovery, but the ROA-volatility denominator can approach zero for stable firms and produce explosive values that a single winsorization pass may not tame, so the ranking risks being driven by the denominator tail rather than the accrual surplus.

Labeling accrual volatility "novel" is inaccurate — it is the Dechow-Dichev/Francis et al. accrual-quality construct, a well-published priced characteristic — and pairing it with a three-year ROA level makes the composite close to a standard quality score plus near-duplicate of the other accrual-stability proposals in this batch.

Cleanly constructed with the two least-overlapping components in the batch and appropriate industry neutralization for both legs, though it remains a straightforward additive combination of two heavily documented anomalies (balance-sheet working-capital accruals and gross profitability) rather than a true interaction.

The expression contradicts the stated hypothesis: with two non-negative rank inputs, NEG(product) is maximized whenever *either* factor is near zero, so low-earnings-volatility firms rank at the top regardless of accrual history and the signal degenerates into a low-volatility/quality proxy rather than the claimed joint condition.
